blogs.title: Why AI Image Models Forget: A Simple Guide to Orthogonal Finetuning
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper’s main idea: how to customize powerful text-to-image models for new tasks without ruining what they already know. This post would explain the problem of finetuning drift, introduce Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) in plain language, and show why rotating model weights instead of freely changing them helps preserve image quality and semantics.

blogs.title: The Geometry Behind Better AI Art: What ‘Hyperspherical Energy’ Actually Means
blogs.description: A visual, intuition-first explainer of the paper’s core mathematical concept. The post would unpack neurons as points on a sphere, explain why the angles between them matter for meaning, and show how preserving those relationships helps keep a diffusion model’s original knowledge intact. Ideal for readers curious about the science without wanting a full math lecture.

blogs.title: DreamBooth, LoRA, ControlNet… and Now OFT: What’s the Difference?
blogs.description: A comparison post that translates the paper’s technical contributions into practical terms. It would explain how OFT differs from popular finetuning methods like DreamBooth and LoRA, as well as control-focused approaches like ControlNet, highlighting trade-offs in quality, speed, parameter efficiency, and inference cost.

blogs.title: How to Teach an Image Model a New Subject with Just a Few Photos
blogs.description: A reader-friendly post focused on the paper’s subject-driven generation results. It would explain the challenge of making a model learn a specific person, pet, or object from a handful of images, why many methods overfit or collapse, and how OFT and its constrained version help preserve identity while still following new prompts.

blogs.title: From Sketches and Segmentation Maps to Finished Images: How OFT Improves Controllable Generation
blogs.description: A practical look at the paper’s controllable generation experiments, covering inputs like canny edges, segmentation maps, and face landmarks. The post would explain how OFT helps models follow structural guidance more accurately, why that matters for designers and creators, and how the paper introduces a smarter way to measure whether control actually works.

blogs.title: Faster Fine-Tuning, No Extra Inference Cost: Why OFT Could Matter in Real Products
blogs.description: A product-focused post about the engineering implications of the paper. It would explore why OFT converges quickly, uses relatively few trainable parameters, and adds no extra runtime overhead at inference. The piece would connect the research to real-world deployment, showing why this matters for startups, creative tools, and on-device AI systems.
